subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Sixth Mass Extinction
description: A 60-second lesson on The Sixth Mass Extinction.

hook.text: Earth has had five mass extinctions. Many scientists say the sixth is happening right now.

buildup.text: Species are disappearing 100 to 1,000 times faster than the natural background rate.

discovery.text: This isn't caused by an asteroid or a volcano. It is caused by one species: us.

twist.text: Unlike past extinctions, this one could be stopped — if humans choose to change course.

climax.text: One million species now face extinction within decades. The window to act is closing.

punchline.text: We are both the cause and the only possible cure.

quiz.question: How fast are species disappearing compared to the natural rate?

details.summary: Scientists warn that Earth is entering a sixth mass extinction driven by human activity, with current species loss rates 100 to 1,000 times higher than the natural background rate. Unlike past extinctions caused by asteroids or volcanism, this one is caused by us.
details.whyItMatters: The sixth extinction is unique because it is preventable. Every policy decision about land use, pollution, and climate either accelerates or slows the crisis.
takeaways: Current extinction rates are 100 to 1,000 times above normal
Vertebrate populations have declined 69 percent since 1970
Human land use, pollution, and climate change are the drivers

faq.question: How do scientists know extinction rates are abnormally high?
faq.answer: The fossil record shows a background extinction rate of roughly 0.1 to 1 species per million per year. Current observed rates are at least 100 times higher, and some groups like amphibians are disappearing thousands of times faster.

faq.question: Is the sixth mass extinction still reversible?
faq.answer: Unlike an asteroid, human-driven extinction can theoretically be slowed or stopped through habitat protection, pollution reduction, and climate action. However, every extinct species is gone forever, and the window for action is narrowing.
